info.title: Castle Escape API
info.description: Authoritative game server for Castle Escape (KTU T120B516). Lobby and inspection over REST, real-time play over the SignalR hub at /hubs/game. Endpoints that act as a player need the X-Player-Token header returned by create/join.

get.description: Tick rate, session counts, and the average and slowest time to tick all sessions once.

post.description: Starts `threads` threads through a Barrier; all read ContentCatalog.Instance at once. Reports distinct instances (1) and creations (1). With `naive=true` the same race against a lock-free holder makes several.

Serializes a real tick state through IMessageSerializer (`format=json|xml`), round-trips it, and counts the members of the 3-member target against the adaptees JsonSerializer and DataContractSerializer.
Spawns items on the tutorial level through ItemSpawners.For(consumable) (`kind=health|reward|power|all`), applies each to a player, and lists the product family (HealthItem, RewardItem, PowerItem).

Creates the product family of each theme factory (`theme=dungeon|crypt|both`): wall, water, pit and zombie with their gameplay values. Then generates a real level of that theme and checks every placed part comes from the same family.

LevelDirector builds level `level` with ProceduralLevelBuilder (random, `seed`) and PresetLevelBuilder (the `preset` map: tutorial or arena), using the same step order. Returns both results as map rows.

post.summary: Prototype: deep vs shallow level copies
post.description: Clones the tutorial level (`mode=Deep|Shallow|both`) and reports, for the level and its parts, the memory address and identity hash in the original and the clone. Then plays on the clone and restarts from the pristine level: deep restores it, shallow does not. The game itself uses `Patterns:PrototypeCloneMode`.

Puts the same zombie behind a wall and swaps its strategy (`strategy=Greedy|Bfs|AStar|Predictive|all`), running up to `steps` steps with each. Greedy gets stuck, BFS and A* go around, Predictive aims where the player is heading. Also compares BFS and A* search cost.

Gives a character (`character=warrior|scout|swimmer`) `sprints` Sprint pickups, then Jump and Swim. After each pickup it prints the decorator chain, its depth and the floor/water/pit speeds. The combos JumpDash and FastSwim are added as decorators too. Then all timers expire and the chain unwinds.

Plays a scripted two-player session. Both players step into the same tile, and the later StartStep command is undone (D7). One player collects a coin, the other restarts the level, and UndoLastCommand() (`undoRestart`) puts the pre-restart level, score and positions back. Returns the command history.

Plays a scripted session with an extra Recorder observer attached: a coin pickup and a zombie hit. Shows what each observer did (client messages, HUD statistics, event log, sound cues), then detaches the Recorder and shows it no longer receives events.

Runs a real session for `ticks` ticks and dispatches its messages through a StateNotifier and an EventNotifier on each of two channels: the polling buffer (states every `pollingEvery` ticks) and a counting channel written for the demo. Shows what each pair sent and one polled message in `format`.

post.summary: Facade: a whole game through GameFacade
post.description: Builds the subsystems once (registry, loop scheduler, content), then plays a full one-level game using only GameFacade: create, join, pick characters, walk both players onto the levers, through the door and onto the exits, to Victory. The same facade serves the hub and the REST endpoints.

get.description: Liveness check. Returns 200 with version and uptime while the server is running.
The last 100 commands (inputs, steps, restarts, given powers), oldest first, with the tick each ran in and whether it was undone (Command pattern). An undone StartStep is a D7 tile conflict.
The last 200 game events, oldest first, as recorded by the EventLogObserver (Observer pattern). Pass `afterTick` to get only newer ones.
Counts of every content type and a hash that changes whenever a content file changes.
At least 3 characters that differ in lives, move speed and jump parameter (PLR-1).
Health (+lives), Reward (+score) and Power (temporary power) items (ITM-1). The `type` field tells the kind; Power items carry a `grant`.
Jump, Sprint and Swim with their duration and the items that grant them; JumpDash and FastSwim with the base powers they need (PWR-1, PWR-2).
Two different active base powers create a super power (PWR-2).
Wall (never passable), Water (needs Swim), Pit (needs Jump) (MOV-2).
Speed, contact damage and the default movement strategy of each zombie type.
The fixed sequence of 10 levels: theme, obstacle/zombie/item counts and spawn tables.
The level at a 1-based position in the sequence.
Hand-made maps in content/presets. Use one with `preset=` on the preview, or for every level with `Generation:PresetLevel`.

Builds level `index` (1-10) with the Builder pattern: the procedural builder for `seed` (validated and retried like in a game), or the preset builder for `preset`. Returns the map rows, the themed obstacles and zombies (Abstract Factory, Strategy) and the validation report. Same seed, same level.

post.description: Creates a two-player session with you as player 1. Share the joinCode with player 2. Keep the playerToken: send it as X-Player-Token and as the hub's playerToken.

get.description: Every session on this server with its phase and player count.

post.description: Joins as player 2. The session then waits for both players to pick a character.

get.description: Phase, players, chosen characters and current level.

put.description: PLR-1. Allowed until the game starts. When both players have picked, the first level loads.

delete.description: Ends the session for both players (phase Aborted); the other player is notified.

post.description: Same as the hub's SetDirection. Send a direction on key down and None on key up. Applied at the start of the next tick.
D8: the level returns to its generated layout; both players' lives and score return to the level start.

get.description: The latest per-tick state: players, zombies, items, levers, door. JSON by default; `?format=xml` or `Accept: application/xml` for XML (NET-2, Adapter pattern).

The same messages SignalR pushes, kept in a per-session buffer for clients without a hub connection (Bridge pattern: the polling channel). Pass the last `seq` you saw as `afterSeq`. Each `body` is serialized as `format=json|xml`. StateUpdated is buffered every `Realtime:PollingStateEveryNthTick` ticks; events are never skipped.

get.summary: Static layout of the current level
get.description: Rows of map legend characters, plus the legend itself.
Per player: lives, score, active powers with time left, combos, statistics. Plus level, levers and door status.
Hub URL and query parameters, every server-to-client and client-to-server method with its payload and when it happens, every event type and error code, and the ordering rules.

get.summary: Example payload of every server message
get.description: Captured from a short real session on a small map, keyed by client method name. This is exactly the JSON SignalR sends.
Name, owner, the problem solved, the course requirement and how it is met, and the participants found in the code by the [DesignPattern] attribute.
Details and participants (type, role, source file) of one pattern, by key, e.g. `decorator`.

post.summary: Two players, characters picked, level 1 starting
post.description: Skips the lobby: creates a session with Ana and Ben, picks their characters and returns both player tokens and hub URLs. Open each hub URL (or the playground) in its own tab.

put.summary: Switch deep/shallow level copies at runtime
put.description: `Deep` or `Shallow` (Prototype pattern). Takes effect on the next level start or restart: with Shallow, collected items stay gone after a restart.

post.description: Undoes the most recent command of the session, or of `playerId` (Command pattern). Undoing a restart brings back the level as it was before it.

put.description: Greedy, Bfs, AStar or Predictive, from the next tick (Strategy pattern). It is a command, so `/undo` switches the zombies back. The tick state shows each zombie's `strategy`.

post.description: Jump, Sprint or Swim, as if an item had been picked up: stacks and starts combos (Decorator pattern). Undoable.
Ends the level as if both players had reached the exit; the next level loads after the usual pause.

doorOpen.description: Whether the exit door is open.

ItemKind.description: What an item does when collected (ITM-1).

joinCode.description: The code from the first player.

obstacleCount.description: How many water/pit patches to place.

obstacleTable.description: Which obstacles the patches use (by obstacle id, weighted).

timeLimitSeconds.description: Kept from the class diagram; not enforced (no requirement).

LevelDefinition.description:
Static settings for one of the 10 levels (the class diagram's `Level`). The generator
turns it into a runtime `LevelState`.

rows.description: One string per row, map legend characters.

obstacles.description: The themed obstacle variants this level uses (one family per theme).

LevelLayoutResponse.description: Static layout of the current level (`GET /api/sessions/{id}/level`).

legend.description: Map legend character of its terrain.

variant.description: Class name of the themed variant, e.g. `PoisonWater`.

requiredPower.description: Power needed to enter it; `None` for walls.

seed.description: The seed of the attempt that produced this level (a retry adds 7919 per attempt).

zombies.description: Zombie class and chase strategy per zombie.

validationErrors.description: Broken generation rules (GEN-1..3, LVL-3, D5); empty for a valid level.

LevelPreviewResponse.description: A level built without a session, for previewing (`GET /api/levels/{index}/preview`).

LevelTheme.description: Visual and gameplay family of a level: levels 1-5 are Dungeon, 6-10 Crypt.

averageTickMilliseconds.description: Average time to tick all sessions once, over the last 200 iterations.

failedSessionTicks.description: Session ticks that threw and were isolated.

MovementStrategyKind.description: How a zombie chooses its next step towards the nearest player.

Obstacle.description: A terrain obstacle. The JSON field `type` picks the subclass.

traversalRequirements.description: The power needed to enter this tile. `None` means no power allows it (walls).

moveSpeedMultiplier.description: Speed multiplier while crossing this tile (e.g. water is slower).

problem.description: The problem it solves in this game.

howMet.description: How the requirement is met here.

doc.description: Path to the pattern's document in the repository.

participants.description: Classes marked with [DesignPattern] for this pattern.

PatternDto.description: One P1 design pattern as applied in this game.

file.description: Source file, relative to the repository.

PatternParticipantDto.description: A class that takes part in a pattern, found by reflection on `[DesignPattern]`.

PlayerStateDto.description: A player in the tick state. `X`/`Y` are interpolated for smooth rendering.

method.description: Client method name, as in SignalR (e.g. StateUpdated).

body.description: The payload, serialized in the requested format.

PolledMessageDto.description: One buffered message: the client method it stands for and its serialized payload.

contentType.description: Format of every `Body`: application/json or application/xml.

latestSeq.description: Highest sequence number returned (pass it as `afterSeq` next time); the request's `afterSeq` if none.

messages.description: The buffered messages after `afterSeq`, oldest first.

PolledMessagesResponse.description: Messages read from the polling channel (`GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`).

PowerCombo.description: A super power that is active while all required base powers are active (PWR-2).

PowerGrant.description: A temporary base power granted by a Power item (PWR-1). The JSON field `type` picks the subclass.

durationSeconds.description: How long the power lasts. Null means the `Game:PowerDurationSeconds` setting.
How long the power lasts. Null means the `Game:PowerDurationSeconds` setting.
How long the power lasts. Null means the `Game:PowerDurationSeconds` setting.

isSuperPower.description: True for JumpDash and FastSwim, which come from combos.

durationSeconds.description: How long a pickup lasts (base powers only).

grantedByItems.description: Ids of items that grant this base power.

requiredPowers.description: For a super power: the base powers that must be active together.

PowerType.description:
Base powers (Jump, Sprint, Swim) come from items; super powers (JumpDash, FastSwim) appear

ProtocolMethodDto.description: One hub method. `Payload` is the message type (server to client) or the argument list (client to server).

queryParameters.description: Query parameters the hub URL needs.

serverToClient.description: Methods the server calls on the client.

clientToServer.description: Methods the client calls on the hub.

errorCodes.description: Every `Error.code` value (also the `code` of REST problem details).

rules.description: Ordering, catch-up and polling rules clients rely on.

RealtimeProtocolResponse.description: How to talk to the game in real time (`GET /api/realtime/protocol`).

levelIndex.description: Current level (1-10), or 0 before the first level.

maxLevel.description: Number of levels in the run.

characterId.description: Chosen character, or null while choosing.

connected.description: Whether the player has a live hub connection.

SessionPlayerDto.description: A player as seen in the lobby.

SpawnTableEntry.description: A reference to content by id with a relative spawn weight, used in level tables.

StatModifiers.description: Multipliers applied on top of a character's base stats. Immutable.

doorOpen.description: Whether the exit door is open.

TickStateMessage.description: Dynamic state, sent every tick while playing.

UndoResponse.description: Result of an undo request: the command undone, or null if there was nothing to undo.

movementStrategy.description: Default way this type chases the nearest player (ZMB-1).

ZombieDefinition.description: A zombie type. Types differ by data and movement strategy, not by subclass.
